## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Masked review (APA's official term; substantively equivalent to double-anonymized) — manuscript body is anonymized so reviewers do not see author identity; a separate cover letter with author names/affiliations is shown to the editor only, not to reviewers. Rejection by one section editor counts as rejection by all three JPSP sections — a rejected manuscript should not be resubmitted to another section. (Verified: apa.org/pubs/journals/psp/submit) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | *(pending — APA has cross-journal transfer for some titles)* |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | No (per APA default) |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | *(pending — typically 1-2 rounds)* |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | *(pending)* |

## Soft Metadata

> [!WARNING]
> **Tier 2 (community estimate)** — Soft Metadata below adapted from publisher-disclosed practices, editorial board statements, and community-aggregator evidence (apa.org, manusights.com, scirev.org) gathered 2026-05. Submission practitioners are invited to upgrade individual claims to Tier 1 via `/ja-validate`. See [SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md](../../../../../SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md) for the Skeleton → Tier 2 → Tier 1 lifecycle.

> **The core value of this entry.** OpenAlex cannot fill any of these — they require lived experience and community knowledge. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidance.

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Medium — cross-cultural quantitative work published (2,097 articles on "Cultural Differences and Values" per OpenAlex), but framings expected to align with mainstream Western personality/social psychology canon |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Low-Medium — non-Western data accepted; non-Western theoretical frameworks less common |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | Medium-High — race, gender, sexual identity, minority-stress papers regularly published with quantitative experimental designs |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Mainstream personality theory (Big Five, identity processes), social identity theory (Tajfel/Turner), attachment theory, terror management, evolutionary psychology, moral psychology (per OpenAlex top-10 topics) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must engage **mainstream personality/social-psychology theory with multi-study programmatic evidence**. APA editorial standard strongly prefers 2–4 studies advancing a single theoretical claim. Theoretical advance must be substantive, not incremental.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Desk reject highly likely for single-study designs without strong theoretical justification; manuscripts that fail to reformat per APA guidelines on revision trigger desk reject without further review.

### Methodological Preferences

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 5 | Dominant — multi-study experimental and survey programs are the journal's center of gravity |
| Qualitative interviews | 1 | Rare — qualitative work has near-zero precedent at JPSP |
| Autoethnography | 0 | Outside scope |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 2 | Occasionally published when proposing testable theory |
| Mixed methods | 2 | Accepted when quantitative dominates |
| Meta-analysis | 5 | Welcomed; PRISMA reporting expected |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | 1 — strict APA-style third-person scholarly register |
| **Expected density** | Almost none; first-person reserved for limitations / positionality statements only |
| **Writing style notes** | APA-style formal academic register; mainstream personality/social-psychology vocabulary; statistical reporting (effect sizes, confidence intervals, mediation/moderation) expected in main text |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewers drawn primarily from the international personality and social-psychology research community — strong representation of APA Division 8 (Society for Personality and Social Psychology), tenure-track and senior faculty at quantitative-empirical programs. Expect deep literacy in social identity theory, identity-process models, attachment theory, terror management theory, evolutionary psychology, and modern statistical methods (SEM, mediation, multilevel modeling). Common reviewer demands: "Where are the multi-study replications?", "Effect sizes and confidence intervals?", "Theoretical contribution beyond effect demonstration?".

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | Mainstream personality/social psychology — multi-study programmatic empirical research | https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/psp |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Medium — strong methodological depth; variance in non-Western or qualitative-methods literacy |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Yes (very strong) — reviewers apply quantitative-rigor heuristics (representativeness, generalizability, replicability) to any non-experimental submission |
| **Discourse community signals (editorial board)** | International social-psychology programs; predominantly US/North American institutions; SPSP affiliations | https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/psp |

### AI-Research Notes (supplementary AI research, 2026-07-13)

> Added as a **supplementary, independent research pass** — it does NOT overwrite or supersede the Tier assessment above. Treat conflicts as a signal to re-verify, not as an automatic correction. Overall `signal_quality` for this pass: **3/5**.

**AI-research finding (policy):** APA-wide policy applies to JPSP: generative AI may be used to draft/edit but its use MUST be disclosed and cited in the Method section; AI cannot be named as an author; authors remain responsible for accuracy of AI-provided content and citations; entering submitted/manuscript content into generative-AI tools is prohibited (breaks confidentiality). Allowed-with-mandatory-disclosure, not a ban and not fully open.

**AI-research finding (positioning — what the journal accepts now):** Original empirical research and meta-analyses in personality and social psychology across three independently edited sections: (1) Attitudes and Social Cognition; (2) Interpersonal Relations and Group Processes; (3) Personality Processes and Individual Differences. Registered Reports are accepted (a 2025 RR on appraisal-tendency/risk judgments was published). IRGP section caps at 5 studies per manuscript.

**AI-research finding (experiential):** Top-tier, highly selective APA flagship; all 4 SciRev reviews ended in rejection and first decisions are typically major-revision-or-reject rather than acceptance. No official acceptance rate is published by the journal. SciRev (n=4) is mixed: editors were praised for constructively summarizing feedback, but one entry flagged an 'outright offensive' reviewer comment; report-quality ratings spanned low (1) to high (4). Sample too small to generalize.

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Single-study designs without strong theoretical or replication-package justification (community evidence: manusights / community-source review 2026-05)
- Reformat-on-resubmit failures (APA editorial practice: desk reject on revision when format guidelines not followed)
- Pure qualitative or autoethnographic submissions
- Failure to disclose AI use per APA publisher policy
- Manuscripts outside mainstream personality / social-psychology canonical framing

### Soft Tax

High for qualitative or single-study authors — typically requires complete restructuring with multi-study quantitative scaffolding. For mainstream-aligned authors, soft tax is moderate: APA-style formatting, multi-study programming, theoretical-advance articulation, and engagement with current SPSP literature canon.

### Best Suited For

- Multi-study quantitative / experimental personality and social-psychology programs (2–4 studies advancing a single theoretical claim)
- Social identity theory, terror management, evolutionary psychology, moral psychology empirical work
- Big Five / personality-process research with novel theoretical contribution
- Cross-cultural quantitative comparative studies with strong theoretical framing
- Meta-analyses of major personality / social-psychology literatures

### Not Recommended For

- Pure autoethnography or first-person reflective work
- Single-case qualitative analyses
- Theoretical / conceptual papers without empirical test
- Cultural-psychology dialogical-self work (better suited to Culture & Psychology)
- Critical / discursive psychology papers (better suited to Theory & Psychology)
- Authors needing rapid turnaround (long APA review cycle is normal)

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin](./personality-and-social-psychology-bulletin.md) | SPSP affiliated; same paradigm; slightly lower acceptance bar; SAGE-published with comparable community |
| 2 | [Self and Identity](./self-and-identity.md) | If the work is identity-focused quantitative social psychology; T&F published; comparable empirical-multistudy paradigm |
| 3 | [Personality and Individual Differences](./personality-and-individual-differences.md) | If the paper is individual-differences focused (ISSID affiliation); broader methodological tolerance |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from a top general-psychology venue (e.g., *Psychological Review*, *Perspectives on Psychological Science*), JPSP is often a better fit because: it specializes in personality/social psychology with deep reviewer-pool expertise; multi-study programmatic packages are the journal's native format; and the SPSP-affiliated audience provides built-in citation community.
